# Native open compound-line controls

Original fixture generated by `tools/open_compound_lines_fixture.py`, using the
original outline-curve control's OPC boilerplate. No third-party document-engine
code or assets are used. Source and native PDF hashes are bound in
`reference.json`; the recorder also verifies that every package part matches
the DOCX actually opened in the reference application.

Four 288 × 216 pt pages contain 48 open custom paths: double, triple, thick/thin
and thin/thick; flat, round and square caps; forward and reversed straight lines
and cubic curves. The physical pen is 6 pt. Frames are 66 × 24 pt and anchors are
page-relative. No dashes, markers, effects, transparency or group transforms are
included in this control.

The reference application opened the exact source without a repair prompt. Its Save As PDF output was
captured on 2026-09-30 with Standard quality. `native.pdf` is the native output;
`tools/record_open_compound_lines.py <work-directory>` extracts its filled vector
contours in physical points with a top-left page origin. These are print/vector
references, not a claim about screen antialiasing. Numeric PDF coordinates retain
the reference application's export rounding.

## Observations and implementation consequences

- Band/gap proportions are 1:1:1, 1:1:2:1:1, 3:1:1 and 1:1:3.
- Reversing the directed open path swaps the thick and thin sides. The existing
  closed-contour interior/exterior clipping rule cannot determine these sides.
- A round cap closes the entire outer end with a semicircle of radius half the
  total pen. Interior gaps terminate flat at the original endpoints. Independently
  round-capping each band, or round-capping the erased gap, gives the wrong result.
- Square caps extend the bands AND their gaps by half the total pen. Using each
  band's own width for square extension gives the wrong result.
- An open curve must retain its authored starting point and remain open. The
  current closed-contour seam rotation and closing segment are inappropriate.

The straight controls have explicit measured band bounds and cap counts. All 24
curved contours are retained for the renderer comparison; straight-line tests do
not prove curve, cusp, join, self-intersection, dash or marker behavior.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.2.2.24 (`ln`) and 20.1.10.15 (`ST_CompoundLine`) define the
declarations. These numeric rendering observations extend the native evidence for
the existing closed-compound implementation. No spec divergence is claimed.

## Status

Open compound paths now import and render with directed bands and native caps.
The browser checks all 48 native contours both directly and through document
import, painting, editing, export/reopen and undo. Reflection/quarter-turn and
half-opacity controls compare transformed native contours. Closed contours keep
their former seam, gap and dash behavior; open contours retain authored endpoints.
The flat/rotated-line branch uses the same band painter.

Compound line-end markers remain explicitly guarded. Their mixed-content unit
control preserves the other 47 drawings in read-only recovery. Explicit zero-width
compound hairlines retain their existing guard. Native controls for sharp joins,
cusps, self-intersections, collapsed contours, nonuniform nested groups and open
dash endpoints remain further fidelity work; this matrix does not establish their
agreement with the native reference. No corpus document is promoted by these controls.
